highlights.title: Google tests buying from Walmart-owned Flipkart through Gemini and AI Mode in India
highlights.summary: The limited test covers select products and users, with a broader rollout planned for later in October.
body: Disrupt ticket savings of up to $200 + 50% off a second ends Sept 25, 11:59 p.m. PT. REGISTER HERE.

Google has started testing a way for shoppers in India to buy products from Walmart-owned Flipkart directly through Gemini and AI Mode, as the search giant looks to expand its AI services from product discovery into transactions.

Users in the test see a “Buy” button on select Flipkart product listings appearing in Gemini and Google’s AI Mode, which takes them directly to a Flipkart checkout flow without leaving the AI interface, according to people familiar with the matter and an experience seen by TechCrunch.

The early test is limited to some users and a small selection of products, including smartphones, electronics, and mobile accessories, the people told TechCrunch. Other users continue to see regular product listings from Flipkart in Gemini and AI Mode without the option to buy them directly from the AI interface.

highlights.title: Alpine to consider what action to take after three-car Colapinto crash
highlights.summary: Alpine chief Flavio Briatore says he will take time to "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after Franco Colapinto's "very poor" error caused a three-car collision in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
body: Attempting to make a bold move from 10th place down the inside into Turn One at the first Safety Car restart, Colapinto locked his brakes and hit the side of team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Lando Norris' McLaren on his outside. All three drivers retired.
Gasly had been running a strong seventh at the time and the incident cost Alpine what stood as seven points overall.

With both Alpines and Norris having dropped out ahead of him, Arvid Lindblad instead came through late in the race to finish seventh and stretch Racing Bulls' lead over Alpine in the fight for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship to 15 points with a scheduled eight rounds left.

Speaking in Alpine's official press release after the race, executive advisor Briatore made clear his frustration at Colapinto's driving, for which the Argentine unreservedly apologised, and said they would work out what to do to ensure lessons were learnt to avoid a repeat in future.

highlights.title: Minecraft still gains around 300,000 new players a day, Xbox boss reveals
highlights.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says Minecraft still gains over 300,000 new players a day, as Minecraft Live reveals Dungeons II and a Switch 2 port.
body: More than 300,000 try Minecraft for the first time every single day.
That's according to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who announced on Twitter/X over the weekend that despite 17 years and 425 million copies sold, "Minecraft is still finding new players".
"Today at Minecraft Live: Dungeons II, our first new dimension in more than 14 years, new ways for creators to build, Minecraft on Nintendo Switch 2, and more," she wrote.

"More than 300,000 people play Minecraft for the first time on an average day. After 17+ years and 425M+ copies sold, I love that Minecraft is still finding new players and giving longtime ones new things to discover."

highlights.title: Supercell’s mo.co heads back into beta as studio plans major changes
highlights.summary: Supercell has moved Mo.co back into beta development after admitting the monster-hunting game is not performing as well as hoped. The current version will remain in low maintenance while the team experiments with new ideas and works on what comes next.... [ MORE ]
body: Despite the company admitting last month that the title will need bigger changes to achieve mass appeal, Supercell said it believes in the game and has more ideas planned for future testing.
“We previously shared that mo.co isn’t performing as well as we had hoped, and it will need bigger changes to get where we want it to be," the company wrote in a post.
“With that in mind we’ve decided to move the game back to Beta. The current game will continue on low maintenance while we focus on experimenting, testing new ideas, and building what comes next."
The current game will not receive new weapons in upcoming seasons, while seasonal passes will lose their premium tracks and weapons.

“I will not use AI in making ‘Mamma Dunhuang,'” Jia says. “It only plays a role in the story.”

Jia founded the Pingyao festival, which marks its 10th edition this year. He says that although it’s only been a decade, “the changes in the broader film ecosystem and the media landscape, as well as technological advancements, are drastic. Pingyao has remained nimble. We’ve been able to adapt continuously alongside the shifts in the film industry and surrounding media, capturing new developments for our curation. Looking ahead, I believe cinema will continue to evolve rapidly, so we will maintain this festival’s agility in the future. That very flexibility allows us to respond in real time to the most pressing cinematic and cultural topics on people’s minds today.”

highlights.title: Some Pancreatic Cells Are Just One Genetic Tweak Away From Treating Diabetes
highlights.summary: By deactivating a gene, researchers were able to cause cells in the pancreatic ducts to produce insulin to regulate blood sugar.
body: A human pancreas typically contains about a billion beta cells, the primary producers of insulin. Among people with diabetes, these cells are either missing or dysfunctional, and thus scientists have been looking for ways to replenish their numbers as a possible long-term treatment or even cure for the condition. A team of researchers recently took a step closer to that reality, genetically altering another type of pancreatic cell to produce and release insulin in response to high blood sugar.

The researchers engineered ductal cells, which—as some previous studies had found—occasionally transform into beta cells all on their own. This is an unusual phenomenon among cells in adult bodies, which tend to be firmly fixed in their identities, and it hinted to the scientists that these ductal cells would be a good place to start.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.

highlights.summary: Congratulations: You’ve almost made it through one of the busiest Septembers in video game history! For anyone who enjoys keeping up with new games as they come out, September has run a ceaseless pace.
body: Those big-name games were only the tip of one gigantic iceberg, though. September was filled with lesser-known indie gems that are worth coming back to if you ever manage to finish Fortune’s Weave. From cozy puzzle games to excellent Metroidvanias, these three September deep cuts make for a much-needed cooldown between hours of hacking and slashing.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

If you’re the kind of person who frequents review aggregate sites like Opencritic, you may have been shocked this week to see that Well Dweller is currently one of the best reviewed games of 2026. That was less surprising to those who are already familiar with the work of developer Kyle Thompson. The mind behind last year’s lovely Crypt Custodian has put together another strong twist on the Metroidvania formula with the fairytale-like Well Dweller. If you’re looking for something that has the vibe of Hollow Knight: Silksong minus the crushing difficulty, Well Dweller is a more approachable 2D action game that’s still complex enough to please fans of the genre.

body: If, for a long time after All Saints’ noughties heyday, the sisters would have known this look was not the height of fashion, things have changed in 2026. Judging by those attending shows at London fashion week this month, camo is very much back.

Worn with heels, beaded flats, camisoles and shirting, camo trousers became a standout front-row trend, one that had first been spotted at Copenhagen fashion week in August. Vogue described it as “a clear winner among the trends we spotted outside the shows”. Fashion editors aren’t alone either: celebrities including Alexa Chung and Iris Law have worn camo recently. And Brad Pitt, promoting his new survival movie Heart of the Beast, looked the part wearing camo trousers and matching jacket this month.

Hetty Mahlich, a brand editor at Burberry, was photographed wearing her army surplus camo pants at fashion week. She likes the way they can give a sense of contrast to an outfit: “They go with a vintage nightdress or a white baby tee, but they’re also great with a heel as I never like feeling too dressed up.”

highlights.title: ‘Mum, where did my Robux go?’ The Roblox scam targeting children
highlights.summary: Criminals are trying to glean login details to harvest players’ in-game currency and personal data. Your 10-year-old son has started playing Roblox, when he realises all of his in-game currency, Robux, is gone.
body: When you try to find out what happened, he says he was recently promised extra Robux if he followed a link on YouTube. When he signed on at the site link, he was taken to the Roblox site as usual but there was no sign of the extra currency.

He has fallen victim to a fraud where Roblox users – many of whom are children – are being targeted for their login details. With those details criminals can steal the virtual currency and players’ personal data.

Within Roblox, players use Robux to buy virtual items, such as skins or animations for their avatar. You can earn the currency within the game, but it can also be bought. At Roblox’s online store you can buy packages costing up to £199.99.
Using ready-made kits bought on the dark web, fraudsters create a fake login page that is identical in appearance to the legitimate Roblox site.

Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah.

A clean sweep in the Friday foursomes gave the visitors a 7-3 advantage heading into Saturday's double session, where the Internationals saw the leaderboard filled with red numbers in both - indicating American leads - before delivering late fightbacks.

The Internationals claimed a share of the spoils in the afternoon foursomes to take a 10.5-7.5 advantage into the Sunday singles, just the fourth time they've led heading into the final day of a Presidents Cup and first experience of it on American soil.

highlights.title: The 10 Best Fights in 'Jujutsu Kaisen' History, Ranked
highlights.summary: MAPPA’s adaptation has continued raising the bar with each successive arc. Season 1 established the fundamentals through Yuji Itadori and Aoi Todo’s exhilarating teamwork and Satoru Gojo’s casual displays of near-godlike power.
body: Jujutsu Kaisen has never treated a fight as mere spectacle. The anime ’s best battles reveal how their participants think under pressure, turning elaborate cursed techniques into tactical puzzles that expose a character’s strengths, fears, and capacity for improvisation. The result is one of the most kinetic battle shonen ever made — and one in which “strength” can mean something entirely different from one confrontation to the next.

That constant escalation makes ranking the anime’s fights difficult. An early confrontation involving Yuji or Megumi Fushiguro naturally feels smaller than the deadly contests awaiting them in the Culling Game, while Sukuna ’s destructive battle with Mahoraga may eventually be eclipsed by what the anime’s upcoming fourth season has in store. For now, however, these are the 10 best fights in Jujutsu Kaisen, ranked from great to greatest for their animation, tactical ingenuity, and character-defining consequences.

highlights.title: ‘I’d like to explain why I was such a monster back then’: six writers on the apologies they wish they’d made
highlights.summary: From making life hell for a young teacher to doubting the motives of a caring foster mother, Olivia Petter, Derek Owusu, Annie Lord and other writers repent for past bad behaviour. At school, I was not a good girl.
body: At school, I was not a good girl. Actually, that’s putting it mildly: I was an emotional terrorist hellbent on inflicting torture and humiliation on my year 6 teacher, Ms Hill, one whoopee cushion at a time. That’s how it began, anyway, but like all crimes, mine followed a strategic pattern of escalation, carefully executed alongside my best friend and accomplice.

We started small: bringing spiders into Ms Hill’s classroom; writing silly notes on the whiteboard; replacing her precious chocolate digestives with stale biscuits from the dining hall. Then we took things further, hiding in cupboards behind her desk and jumping out to frighten her halfway through lessons, and, on one occasion, exploiting the bathroom’s faulty taps to flood the entire thing over lunchtime.

None of this was OK. In fact, it was downright awful, a symptom of reckless malevolence fuelled by boredom and entitlement. We were just unhappy kids who wanted to watch the world burn – an operation that poor Ms Hill bore almost all of the brunt of. To be clear, we never did anything that would constitute harassment, but our pranks were consistent and cruel.

highlights.summary: Meta says Muse is just for adults, though its cuddly, Labubu-like mascot—and upcoming Tamagotchi-style AI device—may be disarming for users of all ages.
body: Meta’s Muse mascot is named Jolly. It's an adorable, cuddly representation of Meta’s AI agent that you can dress however you want—like a doll. At the company’s recent Meta Connect event, CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s furry Muse donned a toga and laurel wreath. In Instagram ads I saw for Muse, the mascot wore exercise gear and boasted about helping with my fitness goals. Later this year, Meta plans to sell a Tamagotchi-style device for your Muse character. It’s all very kawaii-coded.

Although Muse’s ability to complete digital tasks rocketed it to the top of the app charts, its Labubu-adjacent mascot latched this agent onto the cultural zeitgeist. Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, recently posted nonstop memes of Jolly, sometimes in suggestive situations. What remains perplexing to me is why a product for adults—Muse is restricted to those 18 and over—looks just like a well-designed children’s toy.

highlights.title: DC's Groundbreaking 170-Episode Action Series Is Waiting to Be Discovered on Free Streaming
highlights.summary: The CW has produced more than its fair share of DC superhero shows over the years, from The Flash and Supergirl to Legends of Tomorrow and Black Lightning. Some remain favorites in their own right, while others became memorable for just how wonderfully weird the shared universe eventually became.
body: That same ambition extends to the show's special effects and massive set pieces. Although the CGI doesn’t hold up next to modern blockbusters, Arrow regularly attempted large-scale stunts that could have been far more embarrassing on a television budget. What makes such action sequences special is how they’re often inextricably tied to the show's emotional stakes and dual-narrative structure.

Perhaps no scene highlights this better than the epic season 2 finale showdown between Oliver and Slade Wilson (Manu Bennett). The masterful editing seamlessly weaves back and forth between their sword-swinging deathmatch in the island flashbacks and their present-day brawl through Starling City, anchoring the spectacular choreography in years of deeply personal betrayal. Whether he was clashing with formidable villains like Malcolm Merlyn (John Barrowman) or relying on the tactical support of trusted allies like John Diggle (David Ramsey) the action in Arrow was the physical manifestation of Oliver's arduous journey from a hardened survivor to a genuine hero.
points: The CW has produced more than its fair share of DC superhero shows over the years, from The Flash and Supergirl to Legends of Tomorrow and Black Lightning.

highlights.title: ‘I turbocharged my career then pressed eject’: why couples are getting divorced later
highlights.summary: Financial pressures, legal changes and shifting attitudes may help explain why couples are staying married for longer. “We don’t know anyone whose marriage hit the skids after just a few years,” Celia said, reflecting on her divorce.
body: It took Celia two years to initiate divorce after realising her 12-year marriage wasn’t going anywhere – and the latest figures show this experience is increasingly common, with marriages that end in divorce now lasting longer than at any point since records began.

“I approached it very methodically,” the AI analyst said. “I knew that women almost always end up financially worse off after divorce, especially where there are children concerned, so I took the time I needed to turbocharge my career before pressing ‘eject’.”
It helped, Celia said, that she and Martyn, her former husband, had been in their 40s when they got married.

“Because we were older and wiser, we took the time to try to mend our relationship instead of rushing off to start a new life,” she said. “When that didn’t work, Martyn was mature enough to know it was best for the children, me and us that he subtly left me alone to get to where I needed to be before we formally called time on the relationship.”

highlights.title: Where to Get Pizza in Naples, Italy, Home of the Original Margherita Pie
highlights.summary: The best pizza in the city, according to a longtime visitor.
body: Ask 10 Neapolitans about where to find the best pizza in Naples, and you will probably get ten different answers. Nipping down to the pizzeria ‘sotto casa’ (on the doorstep) is a bit like popping into your local pub for a pint, a cheap and cheerful night out with friends and neighbours and a chance to catch up on the local gossip.

Many of these places remain way beyond the tourist radar, but central Naples is stuffed with pizzerias and standards are generally high, so you can’t go far wrong; a mediocre pizza just doesn’t cut the mustard in this food-obsessed city. One rule of thumb is to always choose somewhere displaying the VPN sign outside—this stands for Verace Pizza Napoletana, and guarantees that the pizza will be made according to an exacting set of criteria.

The first pizza margherita was created in Naples in 1889 by Raffaele Esposito at Pizzeria Brandi (still in business) for the visit of King Umberto I of Savoy and Queen Margherita. Topped with red tomatoes, white mozzarella and green basil, it recalled the Italian flag and today, it is the touchstone by which any pizzaiolo worth his dough should be judged; there is nowhere to hide with a margherita.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.
